title.rendered: Master the Code of Conduct for Retail Leasing: Enhance Your Business with Fair Tenancy Practices

content.rendered:
Master the Code of Conduct for Retail Leasing:

Enhance Your Business with Fair Tenancy Practices

Why This Course is Essential:

Stay ahead with the latest leasing guidelines. Learn how to navigate retail leasing agreements with confidence and ensure fair, transparent practices.

What You’ll Gain:

  1. Comprehensive understanding of the Code Of Conduct for Retail Leasing.
  2. Tools and strategies for negotiating fair lease terms.
  3. Insight into tenant and landlord rights.
  4. Practical tips for applying the COC in real-life leasing agreements.
  5. Certificate upon completion to boost your credentials.

Who Should Attend:

This course is designed for retailers, landlords, property managers, leasing agents, lawyers and anyone involved in commercial leasing.

About Course Developer and Trainer

A former lawyer, Ms. Lim Hui Nan is currently the Business Development Director and Chief Learning Officer of Empire Eats Group, a Japanese restaurant-bar group that operates a diverse collection of food & beverage concepts in Singapore since 2009. Ms. Lim is also a graduate of the Advanced Certificate in Learning and Performance (ACLP), and Diploma in Design and Development of Learning for Performance (DDDLP).

Testimonials/Success Stories (What Others Are Saying):

The course was eye-opening! Hui Nan’s concise instruction provided invaluable insights for lease negotiations.

Jolene
Founder at Bluetree Education Learning Centre

Hui Nan’s articulate training style made the session highly informative and enjoyable. Connecting with fellow retailers added extra charm to the experience!

Susan Tay
Owner, The Better Toy Store

Enroll Now (Limited Seats Left!):

Please enable JavaScript in your browser to complete this form.

Course Format:

  • In-person
  • Duration: 8-hour session

Pricing Information:

Course Fee:

Singapore Citizens aged 40 years old and above/Applicable for SME Employer sponsored SGs or PRs; up to $4.50/hr Absentee Payroll Funding, Support applicable (70% subsidy) -$195

Singapore Citizens aged 21 to 39 years/Applicable for SME Employer sponsored , SGs or PRs; up to $4.50/hr Absentee Payroll Funding Support applicable (50% subsidy)-$295

Full Course Fee (incl. GST)-$545

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs):

  • “Do I need prior experience in retail leasing?”

          Ans: No

  • “Will I receive a certificate after completion?”

          Ans: Yes

  • “How do I apply what I’ve learned to my business?”

          Ans: Here are some ways you can apply the knowledge and skills gained from the Contract Development for Fair Tenancy Course to benefit your business:

1.     Review Your Current Lease Agreements: Take a closer look at your existing tenancy agreements and identify clauses that could be amended for better protection and fairness. Use the best practices learned in the course to assess key terms like rent adjustments, lease renewals, and termination clauses.

2.     Negotiate More Effectively: Use the negotiation strategies taught in the course to approach your landlord with greater confidence. Aim for mutually beneficial terms, particularly in areas like rental rates, rent-free periods, or shared maintenance costs.

3.     Incorporate Legal Insights: Ensure you are documenting and managing your lease contracts in line with the latest legal requirements. The legal knowledge gained can help you avoid disputes and ensure compliance with the Leasing Code of Conduct.

4.     Develop a Long-Term Leasing Strategy: Apply the tools learned for conducting market and rental research to develop a sustainable leasing plan for your business. This will help you anticipate future challenges and opportunities.

5.     Collaborate with Legal Advisors: Use your new understanding of lease terms to work more effectively with legal professionals, ensuring that your interests are well-represented in any new agreements or lease modifications.

6.     Leverage SGTUFF Resources: Beyond the course, continue networking with fellow members of SGTUFF to share insights, gather intelligence, and receive support from subject matter experts to tackle specific challenges in your leasing negotiations.

Enroll today in our COC for Leasing course and take the first step towards better, fairer leasing agreements. Seats are limited, so don’t miss your chance to gain valuable insights into retail leasing.

FAIR TENANCY





The Fair Tenancy Pro Tem Committee was formed with key representatives from Singapore’s landlord and tenant communities on 26 June 2020, so as to strengthen collaboration and increase the vibrancy and competitiveness of Singapore’s retail, food & beverages (F&B) and lifestyle sectors.

The result is an industry-led Code of Conduct for Leasing of Retail Premises in Singapore (“Code”) based on the principles of transparency, reciprocity and sustainability.

The Fair Tenancy Industry Committee (FTIC) was set up on 3 May 2021, to be the custodian of the Code and ensure that it provides guidance to landlords and tenants of qualifying retail premises so that fair and balanced lease negotiations can be achieved. It is represented by both landlords and tenants, as well neutral parties to offer a holistic approach when addressing matters related to retail lease agreements.

SGTUFF

SGTUFF is a Singapore-registered SGTUFF Co-Operative Ltd governed under

the Registry of Co-Operative Societies, Ministry of Culture, Community, and Youth.


OUR ORIGINS




Singapore Tenants United for Fairness(SGTUFF) came to life in February 2020 primarily because the Coronavirus pandemic forced business owners from the Retail, Food and Beverage and Services sectors to come together to discuss how to collectively address the issues faced by tenants in commercial properties. There are now 700+ verified frontline business owners in our group representing 600+ brands in 2,600+ retail outlets, occupying 3.5mil+ sq ft of commercial space with a 20,000+ strong workforce.

​

Our Group has been very active in representing the community on engaging with multiple government ministries like Ministry of Trade and Industry, Ministry of Law, working with fellow Trade Associations like Association of Small and Medium Enterprises, Restaurant Association Singapore & Singapore Retailers Association and engaging landlords to give feedback and recommendations on what are the short term and long term measures that will address the core issues faced by frontline businesses. We are also part of the Fair Tenancy Framework Industry Committee. SGTUFF has also started multiple community building and self-help initiatives to form new alliances, new ideas and promote synergies amongst frontline businesses.



VISION

The vision for SGTUFF Co-Operative is to be an advocate for frontline businesses on Fair Tenancy and LL-Tenant matters

as well as to leverage collective community scale and synergies to provide both business cost savings to members and stakeholders.

We hope to build our community to include all frontlines businesses in Singapore and to stand as an indomitable force for Fair Tenancy,

symbiotic relationship with Landlords and as an agent of change to revive and rejuvenate Singapore’s image

as a premier shop & dine destination for tourists and travellers.


MISSION




  1. SGTUFF represents and advocates for frontline businesses (focus on SME and micro and nano-SME) on key common areas of interest especially Fair Tenancy and Manpower matters.

  2. SGTUFF provides meaningful and relevant activities/services to our community in areas like cost savings on shared services, digitization, legal help, business advisory, business synergy/networking and lease/rental information.

  3. SGTUFF reinvents frontline business models in Singapore in the pursuit of successful pivoting or driving further growth in so doing, help to regain Singapore’s status as the premier Shopping, Wine & Dine and Services destination in the world.



VALUES

  • Unity & Comradery of community

  • Fairness & Transparency in all our dealings

  • Accountable & Relevant to our community for everything we do.

  • Positive Engagement with all stakeholders

  • Forward Looking in how we reinvent frontline business models.

  • Mutual Respect


COMMITTEE



TERENCE YOW

Chairperson

After 14 years of corporate MNC experience in Procter & Gamble, Terence founded and is Managing Director of the Enviably Me Group of Companies, which is the exclusive distributor of the Melissa brand of fashion footwear in Singapore, Malaysia, and India.

He is Chairman of River Academy, a charity dedicated to helping children from disadvantaged families have access to quality learning and achieve their fullest potential. He also sits on the Fair Tenancy Industry Committee as a member.

sgtuff.org.sg

ELSON LEE

Vice Chairperson

Elson Lee graduated from NUS in 1999 with an Honours Degree in Economics.

He founded Refresh Group in 2003.Refresh Group currently owns and operates a total of 17
clinics in Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia.

sgtuff.org.sg

KESON LIM

Honorary Secretary

A serial entrepreneur at heart who has acquired businesses across a variety of industries, through which he has gained valuable insights into the challenges and opportunities facing micro and small-sized enterprises.

Beyond his entrepreneurial pursuits, Keson is also an experienced investor and quantitative fund manager, consistently delivering strong returns for his LPs.

sgtuff.org.sg

KINA HUANG

Honorary Treasurer

Kina is a chartered accountant and astute managing director with over 20 years’ experience mainly in the Food & Beverage industry. She is a member of the Institute of Singapore Chartered Accountants since 1995 and has been leading the Tembusu Projects group of companies since 2017.

She also volunteers as member, Honorary Treasurer and in her latest post as Lady Vice-Captain in Warren Golf & Country Club Ladies sub-committee since 2014 until 2023.

sgtuff.org.sg

LIK WONG

Management Committee

Experienced Director with a demonstrated history of working in the outdoor and travel goods industry. Skilled in Marketing Management, Negotiation, Sales, E-commerce, and Sales Management. Strong professional with a degree focused in Business from Nanyang Technological University.

sgtuff.org.sg

PETER CHEN

Management Committee

Dr. Peter Chen is the CEO of Crawfurd Medical group and has interests in preventive primary care through health screening, tertiary care and supporting step-down and elder care. Crawfurd Medical aims to tackle the existing challenges faced in the healthcare environment and come up with innovative solutions to solve current gaps in the system through cooperating with both public and private stakeholders so as to achieve the best outcomes for patients.

sgtuff.org.sg

PHILOMENA CANNON-BROOKES

Sub-Committee Member of the Community and Advocacy Committee

Philomena is a serial entrepreneur and the founder and co-founder of fun, playful, and niche concepts, including innovative ventures such as #Kulnari Mystery Golf, #Quay House, #Power Kids Gym, and #Iscream Cafe.

With over 30 years of experience across sales, recruitment, human resources, and business ownership, she brings a dynamic and results-driven approach to every venture. Her background spans retail operations, franchising, business administration, sales and marketing, recruitment training, web design with content management systems, and full P&L responsibility.

She excels at developing and executing business strategies, streamlining workflows and operations, and delivering creative solutions to complex business challenges. Passionate about leadership development, she has a talent for coaching individuals to think creatively and strategically—encouraging teams to step outside the box and reach their full potential.

sgtuff.org.sg

WILLIE GOH

Sub-Committee Member of the Community and Advocacy Committee

Willie Goh’s gymnastics career began in 2002 as a coach, and he progressed to become a manager before eventually founding and managing his own gym. Alongside his professional endeavours, he has been actively involved in volunteering, notably serving two terms as an Executive Committee (Exco) member from 2007 to 2010 at Singapore Gymnastics, the national governing body for gymnastics in Singapore. Currently, Willie Goh is the owner and director of GymKraft, the largest gymnastics facility in Singapore. Since 2016, GymKraft has expanded its operations into Vietnam.
